# Verify applicable submission rules

Read this for submission compliance, anonymity, formatting, or a full pre-submission audit. This file intentionally contains no fixed page limit, deadline, scoring scale, or required-section list.

## Source selection

1. Establish conference, year, track, and stage: initial submission, revision, or camera-ready. A workshop's rules are not automatically the main conference's rules.
2. Start at the official ICLR site, https://iclr.cc/, and follow the target year's author guide/CFP, FAQ, template, and official OpenReview venue links. Verify the page's actual year and scope; a plausible URL or search snippet is not evidence. Fetch the document itself.
3. Use supplied official instructions as evidence with their provenance. If only an excerpt, cached copy, or user-provided rule is available, label that scope and do not claim live verification. User formatting preferences control the requested deliverable; they do not change official submission requirements.
4. Prefer an explicit official update over an older document. If official sources conflict and no update resolves the conflict, retain both and mark the item pending.

For each consequential rule, record source, access date, year/track/stage, required/recommended status, applicability, and observed manuscript status. Use `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, or `not applicable`. An inaccessible source is `pending`, never `pass`.

## Establish what actually applies

| Area | Questions to establish from official sources |
| --- | --- |
| Length and structure | What counts toward the limit? How are references, appendices, statements, and supplements treated? Are sections or forms required? |
| Format | Which style/template and submission mode apply? What changes to margins, fonts, spacing, page numbers, or line numbers are prohibited? |
| Anonymity | Which identifiers must be removed? What is the policy for self-citation, preprints, code/data links, acknowledgments, and supplement metadata? |
| Submission package | Accepted formats, file-size limits, attachment organization, and required metadata or forms. |
| Research statements | Applicable reproducibility, ethics, asset/license, and AI-use disclosures; distinguish recommendations from requirements. |
| Administrative items | Relevant deadlines/time zones, author/reviewer obligations, and metadata, if requested or necessary for this submission check. Mark items requiring the submitting author's confirmation. |

Do not convert general advice into policy: a five-sentence abstract, fixed introduction length, contribution-bullet count, always-required limitations section, error bars on every plot, or a checklist from another conference is not automatically an ICLR requirement.

## Applying rules

- Compare the actual final artifact to each applicable rule. Total PDF pages alone cannot establish a main-text limit violation when excluded sections are allowed.
- Check anonymity across text, visible figures, links, PDF metadata, and supplied supplements when applicable. An identifier is a finding in the context of verified policy; ordinary self-citations are not automatically violations.
- Recommend content edits consistent with the template rather than modifying official style files or using negative spacing to conceal a length violation.
- Do not make commitments on the author's behalf about reviewer registration, ethics approval, code release, or AI assistance. Record what is documented and what needs confirmation.
- If current instructions are unavailable, finish content checks, list unresolved policy items, and avoid declaring the submission compliant.
